Asymptotic Confidence Intervals for Down-State Survival

Source: R/04_dssc.R
ci_dssc.Rd

Compute two-sided, pointwise normal-approximation confidence intervals using dssc() and vcov_dssc().

Usage

ci_dssc(x, time, down, n, level = 0.95)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

time

A nonempty nonnegative integer vector of discrete time points. Values must be less than .Machine$integer.max; missing and infinite values are not allowed.

down

Integer-valued numeric vector of state positions or character vector of state names giving the non-operational states. Missing values are not allowed. Duplicates are ignored; empty and full state sets are valid. States are used in their order in x.

n

A single finite positive integer: the number of observed transitions used to estimate x$P (a trajectory of length n + 1). Missing values are not allowed.

level

A single finite numeric confidence level strictly between zero and one. Defaults to 0.95; missing values are not allowed.

Value

A data frame with numeric columns estimate, std.error, lower, and upper, giving the point estimate, estimated standard error, and confidence limits. There is one row per requested time, preserving order and duplicates.

Details

The asymptotic normality result is Proposition 10 of Gavrilopoulos, Trevezas, and Votsi (2026). The domain restrictions of vcov_dssc() apply.

Normal approximation

The interval uses the first-order normal approximation for a scalar plug-in estimator described in Remark 3 of Gavrilopoulos, Trevezas, and Votsi (2026). Supply a chain whose transition matrix is the plug-in maximum likelihood estimate from the observed trajectory. The chain must be irreducible. The initial distribution is treated as fixed, so its estimation uncertainty is not included. The variance function returns the variance in the \(\sqrt{n}\) limit, giving the interval $$\widehat{\theta} \mathbin{\pm} z_{(1+\mathrm{level})/2}\sqrt{\widehat{\sigma}^2/n}.$$ Bounds are not clipped to the parameter space. Intervals at multiple times are pointwise, not a simultaneous confidence band. Nominal asymptotic coverage requires a positive limiting variance and the assumptions of the linked variance function. Zero estimated variance produces a collapsed interval; this does not establish nominal coverage at a degenerate boundary. Nonfinite estimates or variances and negative variances produce an error.

References

Gavrilopoulos, G., Trevezas, S., and Votsi, I. (2026). Matrix asymptotic calculus for plug-in maximum likelihood estimators in finite Markov chains. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.17161v2. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17161v2.

See also

dssc(), vcov_dssc(), ci_rel()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(0.4, 0.6), P)
ci_dssc(x, time = 1:3, down = 1L, n = 1000)
#>   estimate   std.error     lower     upper
#> 1   0.3200 0.006531973 0.3071976 0.3328024
#> 2   0.2560 0.010451156 0.2355161 0.2764839
#> 3   0.2048 0.012541387 0.1802193 0.2293807
